channel.title: Pit Wall Weekly
channel.description: Strategy, tech and circuit guides for Formula 1 fans.

item.title: Suzuka preview: the figure-eight that rewards commitment
item.description: The Esses punish a car that is nervous on turn-in, and 130R still separates the brave from the rest. What to watch for in practice, and why tyre degradation will decide the strategy.

item.title: The undercut, explained with lap times
item.description: Pit first, use the grip of fresh tyres, and be ahead when your rival comes out of the pits. We work through a real-looking stint to show when the undercut works, and when the overcut wins instead.

item.title: Active aero in the new regulations: a plain-English guide
item.description: Movable wings on straights, more downforce in corners. Here is how the modes work, what drivers control, and what it means for overtaking.

item.title: How to read a tyre strategy graphic
item.description: Colours for compounds, bar lengths for stints, and the little numbers that tell you how old each set is. Once you can read these, a race broadcast makes a lot more sense.

item.title: Albert Park by the numbers
item.description: A street-park hybrid around a lake in Melbourne: fourteen corners, fast chicanes, and a surface that evolves hugely over the weekend. A lap, corner by corner.

item.title: Why teams bring different wings to every track
item.description: Monaco wants all the downforce it can get; Monza wants almost none. The trade-off between cornering grip and straight-line speed, with a few examples from this season.

item.title: Safety cars, virtual safety cars and red flags
item.description: Three ways to neutralise a race, each with different rules for pit stops and gaps. A quick guide so the next one does not leave you confused.

item.title: Night races: what changes under the lights
item.description: Track temperature drops as the evening goes on, and so does grip. Teams plan brake cooling and tyre warm-up around a moving target.
